paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is shouting at us. God doesn't protect His people with a better wall. He protects them with Himself. The LORD says, "For I will be a wall of fire around it, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within it." (Zechariah 2:5) A man shows up with a measuring line to size things up, and God says the city won't even fit inside walls, because He's got it covered.

And look how close they are to His heart. The LORD of Hosts says, "whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye." (Zechariah 2:8) That's how He sees His people, even the scattered ones who were far from home. Then comes the best news in the passage: "Shout for joy and be glad, O Daughter of Zion, for I am coming to dwell among you," declares the LORD. (Zechariah 2:10)

So what does that mean for you, baker? The thing you need most isn't a stronger fence, a bigger plan or more measuring. It's God with you, and He says He will once again choose Jerusalem. (Zechariah 2:12) Hold on to that, and you can do what verse 13 asks: "Be silent before the LORD, all people, for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling." And the vision isn't over, because Zechariah's still got more to see.
